steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Binary form has two sections (A-B); ternary has three (A-B-A) — the return of A in ternary creates a satisfying sense of completion. | Key Fact: Rondo form features a recurring refrain (A) alternating with contrasting episodes (A-B-A-C-A-D-A) — common in Classical concertos. | Key Fact: Sonata form has three sections: exposition (two contrasting themes), development (themes manipulated), recapitulation (themes return in tonic). | Key Fact: Popular music structures: verse-chorus (alternating storytelling and hook), 12-bar blues (I-IV-V chord pattern), intro-outro-break (framing and variation).

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how structure and form are used in a piece of music you have studied. Use musical vocabulary. | Compare how two different pieces use structure and form. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use structure and form in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
